trackers.name: USDA APHIS — Biotechnology Regulatory Services
trackers.desc: The federal office that authorises the environmental release, import and interstate movement of regulated engineered organisms. The ground moved recently: a court vacated the 2020 SECURE rule on 2 December 2024, APHIS reverted to the pre-2020 regulations at 7 CFR 340, and permitting, notifications and petitions restarted through early 2025. USDA then ran a request for information on a replacement framework, closing 15 June 2026. CAN: find permits and notifications by applicant, organism and phenotype, and follow what replaces SECURE. CAN'T: recover records for organisms exempted while SECURE was in force — by design they generated none. FOR: the framework governing every US release is being rewritten right now, in public, which is the rarest and best moment to be watching one.

trackers.name: FDA — biotechnology consultations & animal biotech
trackers.desc: The voluntary pre-market consultation record for foods from new plant varieties, plus the separate approval route for intentional genomic alterations in animals. CAN: see which developers consulted, on what, and what the agency concluded. CAN'T: prove safety — the consultation is voluntary and rests on the developer's own submitted data. FOR: the word 'voluntary' is doing enormous work in the US system, and this page is where you can demonstrate that in writing.

trackers.name: EPA — plant-incorporated protectants & biopesticides
trackers.desc: Where an engineered plant produces its own pesticide, EPA regulates that pesticide — registration documents, risk assessments and resistance-management conditions. CAN: get the pesticidal-trait assessment and the conditions attached to it, including insect-resistance management obligations growers must follow. CAN'T: address the plant itself, only the substance it makes. FOR: resistance-management failures are documented, enforceable conditions — a rare hard hook in a soft regulatory system.

trackers.name: Center for Food Safety
trackers.desc: US legal and policy organisation that has litigated repeatedly against approvals and deregulation decisions, and publishes the underlying analysis. CAN: find case histories, legal filings, and plain-language breakdowns of what a given approval actually permits. CAN'T: act as a neutral record — it is an advocacy litigator, and reads as one. FOR: if a US approval has been challenged in court, the challenge is very likely documented here first.

trackers.name: USDA ERS — adoption of genetically engineered crops
trackers.desc: The official time series of GE crop adoption by trait, crop and state. CAN: establish, with a government citation, how much of a given crop in a given state is engineered — the baseline for any coexistence or contamination argument. CAN'T: tell you about any specific field. FOR: when you need one number a regulator cannot dispute, it comes from here.

trackers.name: SEC EDGAR
trackers.desc: Every filing by a US-listed company. CAN: pull 10-Ks and proxy statements for Bayer's US entities, Corteva and their licensees — segment revenue, litigation reserves, risk factors naming specific traits or lawsuits. CAN'T: reach private or foreign-domiciled subsidiaries. FOR: a company's own risk-factor section is the most candid account of its exposure you will find anywhere.

trackers.name: CourtListener / RECAP
trackers.desc: Free access to federal dockets and opinions, with RECAP surfacing PACER documents others have already paid for. CAN: read complaints, expert declarations and rulings in seed-patent, contamination and approval-challenge litigation. CAN'T: guarantee every document — coverage depends on what has been pulled. FOR: the expert declarations filed in these cases are often better technical writing than the published literature.

trackers.name: Regulations.gov
trackers.desc: The federal rulemaking and comment portal. CAN: find open comment windows on biotechnology rules, file a comment that enters the record, and read every comment others have filed — including industry's. CAN'T: cover state-level processes. FOR: reading the industry comment on a rule tells you precisely which provisions they want removed.

trackers.name: Federal Register
trackers.desc: Daily record of federal notices, proposed rules and final rules, fully searchable with email alerts. CAN: catch a deregulation notice or an environmental-release notice the day it publishes. CAN'T: tell you what happens after comment closes. FOR: set a saved search on the organism and the agency; this is the cheapest early-warning system available.

trackers.name: USPTO Patent Public Search
trackers.desc: Full-text search of US patents and applications. CAN: read the actual claims over a construct, trait, event or sequence, and follow the assignment record to see who holds them now. CAN'T: tell you whether a patent has ever been enforced. FOR: what a company can assert against a contaminated farmer is written here, in public, years in advance.

trackers.name: USAspending.gov
trackers.desc: Federal contract, grant and subsidy award data. CAN: total up what public money went to a given developer or university programme, by year and agency. CAN'T: capture state or private funding. FOR: publicly funded research that becomes privately owned intellectual property is a documented pattern, and this is where you document it.

trackers.name: OpenSecrets
trackers.desc: Campaign contributions, lobbying spend and revolving-door records, cleaned and cross-linked. CAN: see what an agribusiness firm or trade association spent, on which bills, through which lobbyists, and where those lobbyists worked before. CAN'T: capture undisclosed spending. FOR: the revolving-door pages are the fastest route to the regulator-to-industry career path.

trackers.name: FOIA.gov
trackers.desc: Directory of every federal agency's FOI office, with request routing and annual processing statistics. CAN: file directly with APHIS, FDA or EPA and see their historical response times before you do. CAN'T: force disclosure of material claimed as confidential business information. FOR: a refusal citing CBI is itself a document worth having.

trackers.name: SAM.gov exclusions
trackers.desc: The federal debarment and suspension list. CAN: check whether a contractor or research partner has been excluded from federal awards, and why. CAN'T: cover state debarments. FOR: an exclusion is a finding a federal agency already made about the party you are dealing with.

trackers.name: NIH RePORTER
trackers.desc: Every NIH-funded project, with abstracts, investigators, institutions and dollar amounts. CAN: map who is funded for gene-editing, gene-therapy and engineered-organism work, and trace an investigator's funding history. CAN'T: cover USDA or DOE programmes. FOR: the abstract is written before the paper and says what the work is actually for.

trackers.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
trackers.desc: Registered clinical trials worldwide, including gene transfer, gene editing and engineered cell products, with sponsor, phase and site. CAN: see what is being trialled on human beings, where, and by whom. CAN'T: capture unregistered or offshore work. FOR: the only systematic public record of engineering applied to people, and it names the sites.

trackers.name: USDA NASS
trackers.desc: The federal agricultural census and survey programme. CAN: establish GE crop acreage by state and county, organic acreage, and what else is grown nearby — the numbers behind a coexistence or drift argument. CAN'T: identify individual fields. FOR: a government statistic your opponent cannot dispute is worth more than a stronger claim they can.

trackers.name: Non-GMO Project
trackers.desc: North America's largest non-GMO verification programme, with published standards and a testing protocol. CAN: understand what threshold-based verification actually requires, and find the supply-chain testing infrastructure that already exists. CAN'T: act as a regulator. FOR: verification standards define, in operational terms, what contamination costs a producer.

trackers.name: Organic Seed Alliance
trackers.desc: Research and advocacy organisation on organic seed systems, publishing the periodic State of Organic Seed assessment. CAN: get data on seed-supply concentration and on organic growers' contamination experience. CAN'T: supply seed directly. FOR: their surveys are among the few sources quantifying what contamination does to a farm business.

trackers.name: Regulations.gov — APHIS biotechnology docket
trackers.desc: Every open and closed APHIS rulemaking and notice docket in one place. CAN: see what is currently open for comment from the agency that authorises US environmental releases, and read every comment already filed. CAN'T: cover FDA or EPA dockets — change the agency filter for those. FOR: bookmark this and check it monthly; it is where a deregulation proposal appears first.

trackers.name: Environmental Working Group — farm subsidy database
trackers.desc: Recipient-level US farm subsidy and crop insurance payments, searchable by name, county and programme. CAN: establish what public money flows to the operations growing engineered crops in a given county. CAN'T: link a payment to a specific crop variety. FOR: the subsidy structure is part of why the acreage exists, and it is one of the few US datasets published at recipient level.

trackers.name: PACER — federal court records
trackers.desc: The official federal docket system. CAN: pull any filing in any federal case, including sealed-adjacent exhibits that never reach the free mirrors. CAN'T: be free — it charges per page, though fees below a quarterly threshold are waived. FOR: check CourtListener first; come here only for what it does not have.

trackers.name: Office of Government Ethics
trackers.desc: Financial disclosure reports and ethics agreements for senior executive-branch officials, including recusal commitments. CAN: read what an appointee held, what they agreed to divest, and what they promised not to work on. CAN'T: reach career staff below the filing threshold. FOR: an ethics agreement names, in advance and in writing, the matters an official said they would stay away from.

trackers.name: Hawaii Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: The state agriculture department for the centre of the US seed-nursery industry: Hawaii's climate allows several generations a year, so a very large share of the world's GM corn seed is bred and increased on these islands. CAN: reach the state framework, restricted-pesticide reporting and the plant quarantine rules. CAN'T: regulate the engineered plants themselves — that is federal. FOR: the highest concentration of open-air GM breeding on Earth sits on a small island chain, next to homes, schools and endemic species found nowhere else.

trackers.name: Hawaiʻi State Judiciary
trackers.desc: State court records. CAN: read the litigation over the county ordinances — Kauaʻi, Hawaiʻi and Maui counties each passed measures restricting GM cultivation or requiring pesticide disclosure, and each was challenged. CAN'T: cover the federal appeals, which went to the Ninth Circuit. FOR: this is the clearest US test of whether a county may regulate what the state and federal governments have not, and the answer it produced shapes every county effort since.

trackers.name: CDFA — California Department of Food and Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department, running seed certification, nursery inspection and the county agricultural commissioner system. CAN: reach seed law, certification standards and the county-level enforcement network. CAN'T: authorise or refuse an engineered organism. FOR: the county agricultural commissioners are the officials nearest to any Californian planting, and they are locally appointed and locally reachable.

trackers.name: CEQAnet — environmental document database
trackers.desc: Every environmental document filed under the California Environmental Quality Act, searchable by county and type. CAN: find environmental review for facilities, greenhouses and processing plants, and file a comment inside the statutory window. CAN'T: cover federal actions. FOR: CEQA reaches private projects that need a state or local approval, which is a wider net than most environmental review statutes cast.

trackers.name: Oregon Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department, which runs seed certification and the control-area rules used after the glyphosate-resistant creeping bentgrass escape. CAN: reach the control-area orders, the seed certification standards and the state's canola rules. CAN'T: undo what escaped. FOR: Oregon is where the strongest documented case of transgene escape into wild plant populations happened, and the state's own containment paperwork is the record of how that went.

trackers.name: Oregon Judicial Department
trackers.desc: State courts. CAN: follow the litigation around Jackson County's voter-approved ban on GM cultivation, which survived a state preemption law because it was already on the ballot. CAN'T: cover federal matters. FOR: Jackson County is the standing US example of a county ban that took effect and held.

trackers.name: Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship
trackers.desc: State agriculture department for the largest US corn-producing state. CAN: reach seed law, pesticide reporting and the state's agricultural statistics. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: coexistence arguments need a denominator, and in the state with the most corn the denominator is close to total.

trackers.name: Illinois Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department. CAN: reach seed and pesticide regulation in a major corn and soy state. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: the state agriculture department is where drift complaints are actually filed, and where the complaint record lives.

trackers.name: Nebraska Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department. CAN: reach pesticide and seed programmes, and the drift complaint process. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: dicamba drift complaints across the corn and soy belt are logged at state level, and the counts are obtainable.

trackers.name: Minnesota Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department, with an unusually well-documented pesticide and fertiliser monitoring programme. CAN: reach water-monitoring data alongside the seed and pesticide rules. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: Minnesota publishes more environmental monitoring than most states, which makes it the best place to look for what herbicide-tolerant cropping does downstream.

trackers.name: Washington State Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department, which administers the organic programme and seed certification. CAN: reach organic certification and the seed rules protecting the state's specialty seed industry. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: Washington grows a large share of the world's brassica and beet seed, where cross-pollination risk is highest and growers organise around it.

trackers.name: Texas Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: State agriculture department for the largest US cotton state. CAN: reach pesticide regulation and the seed programme. CAN'T: address federal approvals. FOR: cotton is one of the three crops that make up the overwhelming majority of GM plantings worldwide, and most US cotton is here.

trackers.name: Vermont Agency of Agriculture, Food and Markets
trackers.desc: State agriculture department. CAN: reach the state that enacted the first mandatory GMO labelling law to take effect in the United States, before federal legislation preempted it. CAN'T: enforce that law — it was superseded. FOR: Vermont is the worked example of a state law that worked, that industry could not stop in court, and that was ended by Congress instead. The sequence is the lesson.

trackers.name: CTNBio — Comissão Técnica Nacional de Biossegurança
trackers.desc: Brazil's national biosafety commission: technical opinions, commercial-release decisions and the register of approved events. Brazil is one of three countries holding the large majority of the world's GM crop land, so decisions here carry weight far beyond Brazil. CAN: read the technical opinion behind each release, including dissenting positions where they were recorded. CAN'T: give field locations. FOR: the dissents and conditions in a CTNBio opinion are frequently the most quotable material in the whole file.

trackers.name: IBAMA — environmental licensing & enforcement
trackers.desc: The federal environmental agency: licensing, inspection and the sanctions register. CAN: check whether an applicant carries environmental infractions, and follow licensing where a release touches a licensed activity. CAN'T: substitute for CTNBio on the biosafety decision itself. FOR: an applicant's environmental enforcement history is admissible context in a biosafety objection, and it is public.

trackers.name: Portal da Transparência
trackers.desc: Federal spending, contracts, transfers and sanctioned-company lists. CAN: trace public research money to institutions and firms, and check whether a company sits on a sanctions list. CAN'T: reach state-level spending. FOR: Brazil publishes more procurement detail than most, including the sanctions register.

trackers.name: JusBrasil
trackers.desc: Aggregated Brazilian case law, dockets and legal publications. CAN: find the litigation over CTNBio approvals, including the GM eucalyptus challenges. CAN'T: substitute for the official court portals on procedure. FOR: Brazil's GM tree approvals were contested in court on Convention on Biological Diversity grounds — the filings are the template.

trackers.name: Terra de Direitos
trackers.desc: Legal and human-rights organisation working on seed law, land and agribusiness, and a party to biosafety litigation. CAN: reach public-interest lawyers who have actually litigated these approvals. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: they hold the institutional memory of what was argued and what worked.

trackers.name: INPI Brasil
trackers.desc: Brazil's patent and plant-variety office. CAN: search patents and plant-variety protections covering traits grown in Brazil, and identify the holder. CAN'T: rule on infringement. FOR: Brazil is one of three countries holding most GM crop land, so who owns the traits planted there matters globally.

trackers.name: Fala.BR — access to information
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal access-to-information platform, with a public archive of answered requests. CAN: request CTNBio dossiers, IBAMA inspection records and ministry correspondence, and read what has already been released. CAN'T: overcome a commercial-confidence classification without appeal. FOR: Brazil's access law is strong on paper and heavily used; check the archive before filing.

trackers.name: INCRA — rural land registry
trackers.desc: Brazil's agrarian reform institute, holding the rural property registry and settlement records. CAN: identify rural landholdings around a site, and whether a settlement or quilombola territory adjoins it. CAN'T: resolve contested or overlapping claims, of which there are many. FOR: adjacency to a settlement or traditional territory changes both the consultation duty and who has standing.

trackers.name: Ministério Público Federal
trackers.desc: Brazil's federal public prosecution service, which is constitutionally independent and has standing to bring public civil actions on environmental and consumer matters. CAN: find the public civil actions brought against biosafety approvals, and the route by which a citizen can ask a prosecutor to act — which costs nothing. CAN'T: be directed by a complainant. FOR: in Brazil the most effective challenges to GM approvals have come from prosecutors, not from private litigants, and anyone may file a representation asking them to open one.

trackers.name: IMEA — Mato Grosso agricultural economics institute
trackers.desc: The state's agricultural economics institute, publishing planted area, production and cost data by region and crop. CAN: establish how much soy and maize is grown where, in the state that grows more of both than most countries. CAN'T: distinguish GM from conventional directly. FOR: exposure and coexistence arguments need an area denominator, and this is the one the sector itself uses.

trackers.name: Secretaria da Agricultura, Pecuária e Desenvolvimento Rural
trackers.desc: The state agriculture department for Rio Grande do Sul, where GM soy entered Brazil through unauthorised planting before it was ever legal. CAN: reach the state's agricultural administration and seed programme. CAN'T: rewrite that history. FOR: Brazil's GM soy was legalised after the fact, following years of illegal planting concentrated in this state — the clearest case anywhere of approval following adoption rather than preceding it.

trackers.name: SEMAS Pará — environment and sustainability secretariat
trackers.desc: The state environment secretariat for Pará, which licenses activity across a very large share of the Brazilian Amazon. CAN: reach state environmental licensing, including for plantations and processing. CAN'T: cover federal biosafety decisions. FOR: engineered eucalyptus and the expansion of soy into cleared land are licensed at state level, and Pará is where most of that pressure lands.

trackers.name: Biotecnología agropecuaria — CONABIA / Ministerio de Agricultura
trackers.desc: Argentina's agricultural biotechnology authority, including the CONABIA advisory commission: authorisations for release, the register of approved events, and the rules for confined trials. Argentina is the third of the three countries holding most GM crop land. CAN: find what has been authorised and under what conditions. CAN'T: provide trial coordinates. FOR: Argentina approves quickly and publishes tersely — read the conditions closely, because that is where the substance is.

trackers.name: SENASA — national agri-food health & quality service
trackers.desc: Plant and animal health authority, including seed and product controls. CAN: reach the inspection and certification side of the system, and the registers that govern what may move. CAN'T: rule on biosafety. FOR: seed movement and certification records are the practical route to showing where an authorised event has physically travelled.

trackers.name: INPI Argentina
trackers.desc: National patent and plant-variety registry. CAN: identify who holds rights over the events authorised for Argentine cultivation, including the wheat traits. CAN'T: resolve royalty disputes. FOR: Argentina's long conflict over royalties on saved seed turns on exactly these registrations.

trackers.name: Acceso a la información pública
trackers.desc: Argentina's access-to-information agency and request route. CAN: request CONABIA dossiers, technical opinions and the correspondence behind an authorisation. CAN'T: override commercial-confidence exemptions. FOR: Argentina publishes decisions tersely, so the reasoning usually has to be requested.

trackers.name: Grupo de Reflexión Rural / Naturaleza de Derechos
trackers.desc: Argentine legal and research organisation documenting agro-biotechnology, exposure and litigation. CAN: get case histories and the evidentiary record assembled by people who have brought these cases. CAN'T: act as a neutral record. FOR: Argentina has the longest continuous exposure record of any GM-cultivating country, and it is documented here rather than officially.

trackers.name: Bolsa de Cereales / crop area statistics
trackers.desc: Argentina's grain exchange, publishing planted-area and production estimates by province and crop. CAN: establish how much of a crop is grown where — the baseline for any coexistence or exposure argument in the country with the third-largest GM area. CAN'T: distinguish GM from conventional within a crop. FOR: exposure arguments need an area denominator, and this is the one Argentine institutions use.

trackers.name: SAIJ — Sistema Argentino de Información Jurídica
trackers.desc: Free Argentine legislation and case law. CAN: find the rulings on agrochemical spraying near schools and settlements, and on seed-royalty disputes. CAN'T: cover every provincial court. FOR: Argentine courts have restricted spraying near populated areas repeatedly — those judgments are among the most transferable in the region.

trackers.name: INASE — National Seed Institute
trackers.desc: Argentina's seed institute, running variety registration, seed certification and enforcement against unauthorised seed trade. CAN: reach the register of authorised varieties and the rules governing saved seed — the centre of Argentina's long royalty conflict. CAN'T: rule on biosafety. FOR: the fight over whether a farmer may replant their own seed runs through this institute, not through the biosafety commission.

trackers.name: Gobierno de Entre Ríos
trackers.desc: Provincial government of Entre Ríos, where courts imposed some of the first buffer distances between agrochemical spraying and rural schools. CAN: reach provincial agricultural and environmental administration, and the rules that followed the litigation. CAN'T: cover national authorisation. FOR: the school buffer cases started here and the reasoning has been borrowed across Latin America.

trackers.name: Gobierno de Córdoba
trackers.desc: Provincial government of Córdoba, where a criminal trial over aerial spraying beside a neighbourhood produced convictions. CAN: reach provincial environmental and agricultural administration. CAN'T: cover national biosafety decisions. FOR: Córdoba produced the first criminal convictions anywhere in Latin America for spraying near a populated area, which changed what provincial governments believed they could be held to.

trackers.name: CFIA — plants with novel traits & confined field trials
trackers.desc: Canada regulates by trait novelty rather than by technique, which produces a distinctive record: confined research field trials, unconfined release decisions, and the decision documents behind them. CAN: find confined-trial authorisations by applicant, trait and growing season, plus the reasoning for each unconfined release. CAN'T: capture organisms judged not novel — the Canadian equivalent of the exemption gap. FOR: the 'novelty' test is the argument in Canada, and this is where it is applied on the record.

trackers.name: Health Canada — novel foods
trackers.desc: Pre-market assessment decisions for novel foods, including those derived from engineering. CAN: read the decision summary for each approved food. CAN'T: give you the underlying data, which is held as confidential business information. FOR: the gap between the published summary and the withheld data is the FOI target.

trackers.name: Canadian Biotechnology Action Network (CBAN)
trackers.desc: The national network coordinating research and campaigning on genetic engineering in food and farming, and the closest thing Canada has to a standing public record on the subject. CAN: get contamination case histories, corporate-control analysis, regulatory critiques and current campaign fronts. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: CBAN keeps the institutional memory that regulators do not — including incidents that have otherwise disappeared from public view.

trackers.name: CanLII
trackers.desc: Free, complete Canadian case law and legislation, federal and provincial. CAN: read the seed-patent and plant-breeders'-rights judgments that shaped Canadian law, and every judicial review of a CFIA or Health Canada decision. CAN'T: reach unreported tribunal matters. FOR: Canada produced the leading common-law judgment on patent rights over a plant containing a patented gene; it is here in full.

trackers.name: Open Government — access to information
trackers.desc: Federal ATIP request routing, plus a searchable index of requests already completed. CAN: file with CFIA or Health Canada, and — more usefully — request a copy of a package someone else already obtained, which arrives faster and free. CAN'T: reach provincial bodies. FOR: always check the completed-request index before filing your own.

trackers.name: National Farmers Union (Canada)
trackers.desc: Farmer-member organisation with a long record of opposing seed-patent expansion and plant-breeders'-rights changes. CAN: get the farm-economics argument on seed ownership from the people it applies to, plus a route into organised farmer opposition. CAN'T: act as a regulatory source. FOR: farmer organisations carry standing and public legitimacy that campaign groups do not.

trackers.name: Seeds of Diversity
trackers.desc: Canadian seed-saver network maintaining heritage varieties and a member seed exchange. CAN: find and preserve unmodified lines, and reach growers already doing it. CAN'T: certify or test. FOR: the practical answer to contamination is a clean line held in several places by people who know how to keep it.

trackers.name: Canadian Intellectual Property Office
trackers.desc: Canada's patent, trademark and industrial design office. CAN: search patents over constructs and traits asserted in Canada, the jurisdiction whose supreme court ruled on patent rights over a plant containing a patented gene. CAN'T: cover plant breeders' rights, which sit with the food inspection agency. FOR: read the patent alongside that judgment; together they define what a Canadian farmer's exposure actually is.

trackers.name: Office of the Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner
trackers.desc: Public declarations and investigation reports for federal office holders. CAN: check declared assets and recusals, and read the findings where a conflict was investigated. CAN'T: reach provincial officials. FOR: a recusal is an admission that an interest existed, and recusals are listed.

trackers.name: Registry of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Canada's federal lobbying registry, including monthly communication reports naming the official met. CAN: see which company or association met which official, when, and on what subject. CAN'T: capture meetings below the reporting threshold. FOR: Canada names the individual official in the report, which most registries do not.

trackers.name: Saskatchewan Ministry of Agriculture
trackers.desc: The provincial agriculture ministry for Canada's largest canola and pulse province. CAN: reach provincial crop, seed and land programmes. CAN'T: cover federal approvals. FOR: the organic growers' class action over canola contamination originated with Saskatchewan farmers, and the province remains where the coexistence question is most concrete.

trackers.name: PEI Department of Agriculture
trackers.desc: The provincial agriculture department. CAN: reach provincial agricultural administration on an island where a legislative committee held extended public hearings on genetically modified organisms. CAN'T: legislate biosafety, which is federal. FOR: the PEI hearings are one of the few sustained, formal, public deliberations on this subject held by any legislature in North America, and the submissions are a record of what people actually said.

trackers.name: OGTR — Office of the Gene Technology Regulator
trackers.desc: The strongest release register in the world. Every dealing involving intentional release (DIR) and not involving release (DNIR) is licensed and published, each with a full Risk Assessment and Risk Management Plan, and — uniquely — the locations of active crop field-trial sites are published too. CAN: get licence, assessment, conditions and, for active crop trials, where they physically are. CAN'T: cover exempt dealings, which are not listed. FOR: consultation on a risk assessment and risk management plan runs a minimum of 30 days, is advertised in the Government Notices Gazette and can be pushed to you by email alert — set that up. Note what the statute puts out of scope: trade, marketing, food safety and claimed benefits are all outside what the Regulator may consider, so an objection built on them will not land.

trackers.name: OGTR — GMO Record
trackers.desc: The searchable record of every approved dealing and every GM product notified by other regulators. CAN: confirm, with a citable identifier, that a given organism is or is not currently authorised in Australia. CAN'T: show applications still under assessment — those sit in the consultation stream. FOR: the identifier here cross-walks to the OECD unique identifier and from there to every other country's decision.

trackers.name: FSANZ — Food Standards Australia New Zealand
trackers.desc: The binational food regulator: pre-market approvals for GM food, the approved-food list, and public submission rounds on each application. CAN: file a submission on a live application — the windows are real and are answered on the record. CAN'T: address environmental release, which is OGTR's job in Australia and the EPA's in New Zealand. FOR: the submission rounds are one of the few genuinely open comment processes in this subject anywhere.

trackers.name: AustLII
trackers.desc: Free Australian case law and legislation, federal and state. CAN: read the judgments on GM canola contamination between neighbouring farms, and every review of an OGTR decision. CAN'T: reach unreported matters. FOR: Australia produced one of the few fully litigated neighbour-contamination cases anywhere, and the judgment repays close reading.

trackers.name: ASIC company register
trackers.desc: Australia's corporate regulator and company search. CAN: identify directors, shareholdings and the corporate group behind an OGTR licence applicant. CAN'T: reveal beneficial owners behind foreign parents. FOR: OGTR licences name the applicant entity; this turns that name into people.

trackers.name: Right to Know
trackers.desc: Public FOI request platform — requests and responses are published as they arrive. CAN: file with the OGTR or the agriculture department, and read what others have already extracted. CAN'T: reach state agencies in every case. FOR: the published archive means a well-drafted request only has to be made once.

trackers.name: Gene Ethics
trackers.desc: Long-running Australian public-interest network on gene technology, with a detailed memory of licence applications and state moratoria. CAN: get the campaign history behind Australia's state-level GM crop moratoria. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Australia's state moratoria are among the clearest worked examples of a sub-national ban actually holding.

trackers.name: IP Australia
trackers.desc: Patents and plant breeder's rights. CAN: search what is claimed over the events under OGTR licence, and check plant-breeder's-rights registrations on varieties. CAN'T: address infringement. FOR: pairing an OGTR licence number with the patent behind it gives you the commercial intent that the licence itself omits.

trackers.name: Australian Government Register of Lobbyists
trackers.desc: Third-party lobbyists and their clients. CAN: identify which firms lobby for agricultural-biotechnology clients. CAN'T: cover in-house lobbying, which is the larger share and is not registrable. FOR: the gap in what this register covers is itself worth stating in a submission.

trackers.name: Natural Resources and Environment Tasmania
trackers.desc: The state department administering Tasmania's moratorium on the commercial release of GM organisms, in place since 2001 and repeatedly extended. CAN: reach the moratorium instrument, its reviews and the market-access reasoning behind it. CAN'T: override a federal OGTR licence for research. FOR: Tasmania justifies its moratorium on marketing and brand grounds rather than safety, which sidesteps the argument industry is best equipped to win.

trackers.name: PIRSA — Primary Industries and Regions SA
trackers.desc: The state department that ran South Australia's GM crop moratorium and, when the mainland moratorium ended, retained it for Kangaroo Island. CAN: reach the designated-area rules and the reviews that led to the split outcome. CAN'T: cover federal licensing. FOR: Kangaroo Island is the clearest surviving case of a moratorium kept for a defined area after the wider one was lifted.

trackers.name: DPIRD — Primary Industries and Regional Development
trackers.desc: The state agriculture department. CAN: reach the state's GM canola rules and the organic and seed certification frameworks around them. CAN'T: resolve a private dispute. FOR: Western Australia produced the fully litigated neighbour-contamination case in which an organic grower lost certification after GM canola swathes blew onto his land — the state framework is the backdrop to that judgment.

trackers.name: NSW Department of Primary Industries
trackers.desc: State department of primary industries. CAN: reach the state's GM crop legislation, its expert committee and the exemption orders issued under it. CAN'T: cover federal licensing. FOR: New South Wales operated a moratorium and then repealed it, and the repeal debate is the fullest Australian record of the arguments on both sides.

trackers.name: EPA New Zealand — new organisms
trackers.desc: Applications and decisions on new organisms, covering containment, field test and release, with full published decision reasoning. CAN: read the decision-making committee's reasoning in unusual detail, including how it weighed cultural and Treaty considerations. CAN'T: cover food approvals, which run through FSANZ. FOR: New Zealand's decisions are among the best-reasoned public documents in this field, and are useful as persuasive material well outside New Zealand.

trackers.name: GE-Free New Zealand
trackers.desc: Long-running national campaign network on genetic engineering, with a detailed memory of past applications, trials and contamination incidents in New Zealand. CAN: find case history and the local organising picture. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: New Zealand's regulatory record is strong but its campaign history is where the practical lessons are kept.

trackers.name: NZLII
trackers.desc: Free New Zealand case law and legislation. CAN: read decisions on new-organism applications and the judicial reviews of them. CAN'T: cover all tribunal material. FOR: New Zealand's decisions weigh Treaty and cultural considerations explicitly, which makes them persuasive well outside New Zealand.

trackers.name: FYI.org.nz
trackers.desc: Public Official Information Act request platform, with requests and responses published. CAN: request EPA application files and advisory-committee material. CAN'T: overcome commercial-confidence withholding. FOR: New Zealand's OIA is relatively strong and the published archive compounds.

trackers.name: Companies Office
trackers.desc: New Zealand's company register, free and complete. CAN: identify directors and shareholders behind an applicant. CAN'T: reach offshore parents. FOR: small jurisdiction, thorough register — corporate structure here is unusually easy to establish.

trackers.name: Land Information New Zealand
trackers.desc: New Zealand's land titles and survey authority. CAN: resolve a site to a title and identify the owner and neighbours. CAN'T: be entirely free for title extracts. FOR: New Zealand's containment approvals often specify a site, and this turns that into a parcel.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment, Forest & Climate Change — GEAC
trackers.desc: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee sits under this ministry and approves confined field trials and commercial releases, publishing its decisions as meeting minutes rather than as a database. CAN: read what was approved, for whom, in which states and seasons — if you are willing to work through minutes. CAN'T: query it like a register; there is no structured endpoint, which is why India's releases are hard to map. FOR: India is where the gap between a real public record and a usable public record is clearest.

trackers.name: Coalition for a GM-Free India
trackers.desc: The national coalition tracking approvals, trials and litigation, and the main aggregator of documents obtained under India's Right to Information Act. CAN: get RTI-obtained material that is not published anywhere official, plus trial locations reconstructed from minutes. CAN'T: substitute for the official file. FOR: in India the campaign record is frequently more complete than the government's own published record, because of sustained RTI work.

trackers.name: Indian Kanoon
trackers.desc: Free, searchable Indian case law across the Supreme Court and High Courts. CAN: read the Supreme Court proceedings on GM crop field trials and the Technical Expert Committee reports filed in them. CAN'T: cover tribunal matters completely. FOR: India's apex court has engaged with biosafety evidence more directly than almost any other, and the record is public.

trackers.name: RTI Online
trackers.desc: The central Right to Information filing portal. CAN: request GEAC minutes, trial locations, biosafety data and correspondence — the route by which most of what is known about Indian trials became known. CAN'T: reach state bodies through the same portal. FOR: in India the campaign record is often more complete than the official published record, and RTI is why.

trackers.name: MCA company master data
trackers.desc: India's corporate registry. CAN: identify directors, shareholding and group structure of seed and biotechnology companies operating in India. CAN'T: reach unregistered entities. FOR: the joint-venture structures used to enter the Indian seed market are visible here.

trackers.name: Gene Campaign
trackers.desc: Research and advocacy organisation on genetic resources, farmers' rights and biosafety, active since before the Indian regime existed. CAN: get the farmers'-rights and access-and-benefit-sharing argument developed in an Indian legal context. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: India legislated farmers' rights explicitly; this is the organisation that pushed for it.

trackers.name: Navdanya
trackers.desc: Seed-saver network running community seed banks across Indian states and campaigning on seed sovereignty. CAN: reach an operating network of community seed banks and the growers running them. CAN'T: certify or test. FOR: the largest practical seed-conservation network in the region.

trackers.name: Bhoomi / state land records portals
trackers.desc: The land resources department, which coordinates the state-run digitised land-record programmes. CAN: reach the route into a state's land-record portal, which is where Indian parcel data actually lives. CAN'T: offer a single national search — land is a state subject and every state runs its own system. FOR: Indian trial locations are given by district in GEAC minutes, and the state portal is the only way to go finer than that.

trackers.name: Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority
trackers.desc: The statutory authority under India's plant variety law, which is unusual in the world for registering farmers' varieties alongside breeders' and for recognising farmers' rights explicitly. CAN: register a farmers' variety, search what has been registered, and read the benefit-sharing provisions. CAN'T: address biosafety. FOR: India legislated a right that most countries only debate — this is where it is actually exercised.

trackers.name: Department of Agriculture, Maharashtra
trackers.desc: State agriculture department for India's largest cotton state, where Bt cotton adoption and the herbicide-tolerant cotton that was never approved are both concentrated. CAN: reach the state agricultural administration and its seed regulation. CAN'T: approve or refuse an event — that is federal. FOR: unapproved herbicide-tolerant cotton has been planted at scale here for years, which makes state enforcement records the record of what happens when approval is simply bypassed.

trackers.name: Department of Agriculture, Farmers Welfare & Co-operation
trackers.desc: State agriculture department for a major cotton and groundnut state. CAN: reach state seed regulation and the agricultural extension network. CAN'T: cover federal approvals. FOR: Gujarat is where India's first unapproved Bt cotton was found growing before any approval existed — the pattern that has repeated with every trait since.

trackers.name: Department of Agriculture, Karnataka
trackers.desc: State agriculture department. CAN: reach state seed and extension programmes. CAN'T: cover federal approvals. FOR: Karnataka has been a centre of farmer organising against seed patents since the 1990s, and the state administration is the counterpart those movements deal with.

trackers.name: CIBIOGEM — Comisión Intersecretarial de Bioseguridad de los OGM
trackers.desc: Mexico's inter-ministerial biosafety commission, holding the national register of permits for experimental, pilot and commercial release. The constitutional position changed in 2025: after a USMCA dispute panel ruled against Mexico's maize decree on 20 December 2024, Mexico amended Articles 4 and 27 of its Constitution instead, published 17 March 2025, prohibiting the planting of genetically modified maize. CAN: find permit applications and decisions, and the framework they sit under. CAN'T: resolve the trade dispute that follows from moving a prohibition from a decree into the Constitution. FOR: Mexico is a centre of origin for maize, and it is now the clearest test anywhere of a constitutional prohibition set against a trade-agreement ruling.

trackers.name: SENASICA — plant health & agri-food safety
trackers.desc: Plant-health authority handling inspection, seed movement and phytosanitary control. CAN: reach the enforcement and movement-control side. CAN'T: rule on biosafety. FOR: how material physically moves is the practical question in a centre-of-origin contamination argument.

trackers.name: Plataforma Nacional de Transparencia
trackers.desc: Mexico's national transparency platform: file information requests to any federal or state body, and search requests already answered. CAN: obtain permit files, inspection records and internal correspondence from CIBIOGEM, SENASICA and SEMARNAT. CAN'T: overcome a reserved-information classification without appeal. FOR: Mexico's access regime is stronger than most in the region and is used heavily on this subject.

trackers.name: Semillas de Vida
trackers.desc: Civil-society organisation working on native maize, seed sovereignty and the legal defence of centres of origin. CAN: reach the campesino and legal networks behind Mexico's native-maize litigation, and get the case history. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: the maize collective action is the most significant centre-of-origin litigation anywhere, and this is a route into it.

trackers.name: CONABIO
trackers.desc: The national biodiversity commission, which maintains the mapping of maize races and centres of origin and diversity. CAN: get the official geographic basis for what counts as a centre of origin — the map any release decision inside one has to answer to. CAN'T: issue or refuse permits. FOR: a government body's own map of what is irreplaceable is a strong document to put in front of that government.

trackers.name: Suprema Corte de Justicia de la Nación
trackers.desc: Mexico's supreme court, publishing judgments and the record of the collective actions over transgenic maize. CAN: follow the litigation that has suspended permits for planting GM maize, through its many appeals. CAN'T: cover lower federal courts completely. FOR: the maize collective action is the longest-running centre-of-origin case anywhere and the procedural history is the useful part.

trackers.name: IMPI — Instituto Mexicano de la Propiedad Industrial
trackers.desc: Mexico's industrial property office. CAN: search patents in force covering traits and processes relevant to Mexican agriculture. CAN'T: cover plant variety rights, which sit with the agriculture ministry. FOR: what is patented in a centre of origin is a different question from what is patented elsewhere, and it is rarely asked.

trackers.name: Registro Agrario Nacional
trackers.desc: Mexico's agrarian registry, holding the records of ejido and comunidad land — the collective tenure covering a very large share of Mexican farmland. CAN: establish whether ground near a release site is collectively held, and by which assembly. CAN'T: cover private freehold, which sits in state registries. FOR: collective tenure changes the consultation question entirely: an ejido assembly is a decision-making body, not a neighbour.

trackers.name: Gobierno del Estado de Oaxaca
trackers.desc: State government of Oaxaca, where the first reported transgene presence in Mexican maize landraces was found and where a very large share of the country's maize diversity is held by Indigenous and campesino communities. CAN: reach state agricultural and Indigenous-affairs offices, and the state's own position on native maize. CAN'T: decide federal permits. FOR: Oaxaca is not a place where maize is grown so much as the place it comes from, and the state has legislated on that basis.

trackers.name: Gobierno del Estado de Chiapas
trackers.desc: State government of Chiapas, one of the states to declare itself free of transgenic maize. CAN: reach the state declaration and the agricultural offices administering it. CAN'T: override federal permitting. FOR: several Mexican states declared themselves GM-maize-free before the federal position hardened, and those declarations are the local precedent.

trackers.name: Gobierno del Estado de Sinaloa
trackers.desc: State government of Sinaloa, Mexico's largest commercial maize producer and the centre of the industrial-agriculture argument against restrictions. CAN: reach the state's agricultural administration and production statistics. CAN'T: be treated as a neutral party in the maize debate. FOR: the argument for transgenic maize in Mexico is made from Sinaloa, and understanding it is more useful than ignoring it.

trackers.name: BVL — Bundesamt für Verbraucherschutz und Lebensmittelsicherheit
trackers.desc: The German competent authority for genetic engineering, including the location register of deliberate-release sites and the register of genetic-engineering facilities. CAN: find where releases have been notified, at a level of geographic detail most countries do not publish. CAN'T: decide EU-wide authorisations, which run through the Commission and EFSA. FOR: Germany's site register is one of the few in Europe that will actually put a release on a map.

trackers.name: Testbiotech
trackers.desc: Independent institute that systematically re-reads EFSA and national risk assessments and publishes point-by-point critiques, in English and German. CAN: get a technical, citable critique of the exact dossier you are objecting to — often the fastest route to the specific weakness in an assessment. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: if you need one expert source to strengthen a submission on an EU application, start here.

trackers.name: FragDenStaat
trackers.desc: Public information-request platform for German federal and state bodies, with responses published. CAN: request BVL site-register detail, risk assessments and ministry correspondence. CAN'T: reach material held as trade secret without challenge. FOR: German site registers are unusually detailed; the requests fill in what they omit.

trackers.name: Unternehmensregister
trackers.desc: The official German company register and publication platform. CAN: obtain accounts, group structure and statutory publications for German entities. CAN'T: be searched as freely as some registers. FOR: the parent-subsidiary structure of the largest agricultural biotechnology group is German.

trackers.name: DPMA
trackers.desc: The German patent and trade mark office, with DPMAregister search. CAN: search national and European patents in force in Germany over plants, traits and processes. CAN'T: cover pending EPO oppositions in detail. FOR: European opposition proceedings against patents on plants have been a genuinely effective tactic, and they start here.

trackers.name: Save Our Seeds
trackers.desc: Berlin-based initiative on seed purity, patent opposition and EU biotechnology policy. CAN: reach the coalition that has run patent oppositions and EU-level campaigns for two decades. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: they coordinate the No Patents on Seeds work, which is the most concrete counter-move to trait ownership in Europe.

trackers.name: Umweltinstitut München
trackers.desc: Independent environmental institute with its own laboratory, long active on agriculture and gene technology. CAN: reach independent testing capacity and technical critique. CAN'T: substitute for an accredited certifying lab. FOR: an institute that runs its own lab can say things a campaign group cannot.

trackers.name: BUND
trackers.desc: Friends of the Earth Germany, with an established gene-technology programme and regional groups. CAN: find local organising capacity and the German position papers on EU deregulation. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: regional structure means there is usually a group near a notified release site.

trackers.name: Standorttregister — GMO location register (BVL)
trackers.desc: Germany's statutory public register of sites where GMOs are released or cultivated, searchable by location. CAN: find the actual parcel-level location of a notified release — something almost no other country publishes. CAN'T: cover contained-use facilities at the same granularity. FOR: this register exists because German law requires it, and it is the strongest argument available that publishing release locations is both possible and lawful.

trackers.name: Rechtsprechung im Internet
trackers.desc: Free decisions of the German federal courts. CAN: read the federal administrative and constitutional rulings on gene-technology law, including on the location register and on liability between neighbouring farms. CAN'T: cover state courts. FOR: German law imposes strict liability on the GMO user for damage to a neighbouring crop — the case law interpreting that is here.

trackers.name: Lobbyregister des Bundestages
trackers.desc: Germany's statutory lobbying register, with declared expenditure, clients and areas of interest. CAN: see what an agricultural or biotechnology interest spends and on which legislative files. CAN'T: predate 2022, when the register began. FOR: German entries are unusually detailed on expenditure bands, which makes comparison across firms possible.

trackers.name: Bavarian State Ministry for the Environment
trackers.desc: The Bavarian environment ministry. CAN: reach the state framework of a Länd that declared itself a GM-free region and pressed for national cultivation bans. CAN'T: override federal or EU authorisation. FOR: Bavaria is the largest single member of the European GMO-free regions network, and its declaration is the template most others followed.

trackers.name: Ministry of Climate Protection, Agriculture and Environment
trackers.desc: The state ministry for agriculture and environment. CAN: reach the state that hosted most of Germany's commercial GM maize cultivation before it ended nationally. CAN'T: cover federal registers. FOR: this is where German GM cultivation actually happened, which makes the state's own record the best account of why it stopped.

trackers.name: ACRE — Advisory Committee on Releases to the Environment
trackers.desc: The statutory advisory committee on releasing genetically modified and other novel organisms, with published advice and meeting papers. CAN: read the advice given to ministers on specific applications, and the reasoning behind it. CAN'T: capture organisms moved outside the GMO regime by precision-breeding legislation — an actively widening gap in England. FOR: the committee's own minuted uncertainties are the most useful material in the file.

trackers.name: GM Freeze
trackers.desc: UK campaign coalition on genetic engineering in food and farming, tracking applications, trials and legislative change. CAN: find the current UK regulatory fight in plain language, and who else is in it. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: the UK's regime is changing quickly, and the campaign trackers are usually ahead of the government's own explanatory material.

trackers.name: Companies House
trackers.desc: Free, complete UK company register with filing history and persons of significant control. CAN: identify the real owners behind an applicant, follow annual accounts, and see charges over assets. CAN'T: reach offshore parents beyond the PSC declaration. FOR: the PSC register is one of the few beneficial-ownership records in the world that is genuinely free and genuinely public.

trackers.name: BAILII
trackers.desc: Free British and Irish case law. CAN: read judicial reviews of ACRE and DEFRA decisions and the precedent on consultation adequacy. CAN'T: cover every first-instance matter. FOR: UK administrative-law precedent on inadequate consultation is cited far beyond the UK.

trackers.name: WhatDoTheyKnow
trackers.desc: Public FOI platform; every request and response is published. CAN: request ACRE papers, DEFRA correspondence and FSA assessments, and read thousands already answered. CAN'T: force disclosure of commercially confidential material. FOR: search the archive first — on this subject a great deal has already been extracted.

trackers.name: HM Land Registry
trackers.desc: England and Wales title and ownership records, searchable per title for a small fee. CAN: turn a trial site into named owners and adjoining titles. CAN'T: cover Scotland or Northern Ireland (separate registers). FOR: identifying the neighbours inside a drift radius starts here.

trackers.name: Beyond GM
trackers.desc: UK organisation tracking gene-editing deregulation and the precision-breeding legislation. CAN: follow, in plain language, how organisms are being moved outside GMO registration in England — the largest structural gap on this map. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: they track the deregulation file more closely than anyone else in the UK.

trackers.name: Soil Association
trackers.desc: The UK's main organic certifier and a standards body with a formal position on GM and gene editing. CAN: understand what contamination costs a certified producer, and reach the certified-grower constituency. CAN'T: regulate. FOR: certifiers hold the commercial definition of contamination, which is often more usable than the legal one.

trackers.name: Intellectual Property Office
trackers.desc: UK patents and plant variety rights. CAN: search claims and rights over traits and varieties marketed in the UK. CAN'T: address EU-wide rights post-Brexit. FOR: the UK and EU rights regimes have diverged; check both.

trackers.name: Scotland's Land Information Service / Registers of Scotland
trackers.desc: Scotland's land and property registers, separate from the English system. CAN: identify ownership of a site in Scotland, which has maintained a GM-free cultivation position distinct from England's. CAN'T: cover England, Wales or Northern Ireland. FOR: the UK's four nations have diverged sharply on gene-editing law, so which one a site sits in now changes the answer.

trackers.name: Register of Members' Financial Interests
trackers.desc: Declared financial interests of every MP — outside employment, gifts, donations, shareholdings and sponsored travel. CAN: check whether an MP speaking on gene-editing legislation has a declared interest in the sector. CAN'T: capture undeclared interests or those of officials rather than members. FOR: a declared interest sitting beside a vote is a fact you can publish without inference.

trackers.name: ACOBA — Advisory Committee on Business Appointments
trackers.desc: Rulings on jobs former ministers and senior civil servants may take, published case by case with the conditions imposed. CAN: trace the revolving door directly — who left which department for which company, and what the committee said about it. CAN'T: stop an appointment; its powers are advisory. FOR: this is the rare public record of a regulator's staff moving to the industry they regulated, written down by the government itself.

trackers.name: ANSES — Agence nationale de sécurité sanitaire
trackers.desc: The national agency carrying out risk assessment on genetically modified organisms for food, feed and environmental release, publishing its opinions in full. CAN: read detailed French assessments, which frequently diverge from EFSA's and are cited across Europe when they do. CAN'T: make the authorisation decision. FOR: a divergence between two competent authorities on the same dossier is one of the strongest things you can put in front of a decision-maker.

trackers.name: Inf'OGM
trackers.desc: France's dedicated GMO and seed watchdog, publishing detailed technical and legal analysis in French and English. CAN: follow European approvals, deregulation files and national decisions with a level of legal precision almost nothing else matches. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: for anything touching EU GMO law, start here before the primary sources.

trackers.name: Légifrance
trackers.desc: Official French law, regulation and case law. CAN: read the Conseil d'État decisions on gene-edited organisms and national safeguard measures. CAN'T: cover administrative practice. FOR: France referred the gene-editing classification question that shaped EU law; the domestic litigation is here.

trackers.name: Annuaire des entreprises
trackers.desc: The official free French company directory, built on the national business register. CAN: identify company structure, officers and filed accounts. CAN'T: reach foreign parents. FOR: free and complete, which is not true of every European register.

trackers.name: CADA
trackers.desc: The commission that rules on refused administrative-document requests. CAN: appeal a refusal to disclose an assessment file, and read prior opinions on similar refusals. CAN'T: compel disclosure directly — its opinions are advisory. FOR: a CADA opinion in your favour changes the posture of the body refusing you.

trackers.name: Réseau Semences Paysannes
trackers.desc: Network of farmers and gardeners maintaining and exchanging peasant seed, and a party to the legal argument over seed marketing rules. CAN: reach the practical seed-sovereignty movement and its legal position. CAN'T: certify. FOR: French seed-marketing law is among the most restrictive in Europe, and this network has been contesting it for decades.

trackers.name: Confedération paysanne
trackers.desc: Farmers' union with a formal position against GM crops and gene-edited deregulation, and a history of direct action and litigation. CAN: reach organised farmer opposition with legal standing. CAN'T: act as a neutral source. FOR: it was this union's litigation that produced the European ruling on mutagenesis.

trackers.name: HATVP — High Authority for Transparency in Public Life
trackers.desc: Declarations of interests and assets for French officials, and the register of lobbying representatives. CAN: check what an official or an adviser declared, and what a company reported spending to influence a decision. CAN'T: reach undeclared activity. FOR: France publishes interest declarations at a level of detail most countries do not, which makes conflict-of-interest work unusually tractable here.

trackers.name: Cadastre
trackers.desc: France's open cadastral parcel data, downloadable and mappable. CAN: turn a commune and locality into actual parcels, and map a drift radius against them. CAN'T: name the owner — that requires a separate request. FOR: the geometry is free and open, which is enough to identify who to knock on the door of.

trackers.name: Federal Ministry — gene technology & biosafety
trackers.desc: Austria has been among the most restrictive EU member states on GM cultivation and has repeatedly invoked national safeguard measures. CAN: reach the national framework and the reasoning behind Austrian restrictions. CAN'T: be assumed current — Austrian ministries have been reorganised more than once, so confirm the responsible department before citing. FOR: Austria's safeguard reasoning is the standing template for a member state refusing a cultivation approval.

trackers.name: Data.gv.at / Transparenzportal
trackers.desc: Austria's open-data portal. CAN: reach official datasets underpinning Austria's restrictive position. CAN'T: substitute for the ministry on permits. FOR: Austria's safeguard reasoning is the standing template for a member state refusing a cultivation approval.

trackers.name: Global 2000
trackers.desc: Friends of the Earth Austria, central to Austria's long-standing GM-free position and to its testing and labelling work. CAN: get the campaign and technical history behind one of Europe's strongest national refusals. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Austria is the clearest case of sustained public opposition producing a durable national policy.

trackers.name: AGES — Austrian Agency for Health and Food Safety
trackers.desc: The national agency running food, feed and seed testing, including GM analysis. CAN: reach official testing capacity and published monitoring results in a country that tests seed lots systematically. CAN'T: set policy. FOR: Austria's seed monitoring is why its GM-free position is enforceable rather than declaratory — the testing is the mechanism.

trackers.name: African Centre for Biodiversity
trackers.desc: The leading independent research and advocacy organisation on genetic engineering, seed law and corporate concentration across the African continent, with a deep archive of objections, appeals and analyses. CAN: get country-by-country analysis of biosafety law, seed law and specific approvals across Africa — material that exists nowhere else in consolidated form. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: for most of the continent this is the single most useful starting point on this map.

trackers.name: Department of Agriculture — GMO Act registrar
trackers.desc: South Africa's competent authority under its GMO Act: permits for trial and commercial release, and the public objection process attached to them. CAN: file an objection to a permit application, which South African law provides for explicitly. CAN'T: be relied on for a clean machine-readable register. FOR: South Africa is the largest GM cultivator on the continent, and its objection right is real and used.

trackers.name: SAFLII
trackers.desc: Free Southern African case law. CAN: read the appeals and reviews brought against GMO Act decisions, including the successful ones. CAN'T: cover every tribunal matter. FOR: South Africa's GMO Act provides an explicit objection and appeal route, and it has been used and won.

trackers.name: CIPC
trackers.desc: South Africa's company and intellectual property commission. CAN: identify directors and shareholdings of applicants, and search patents and plant-breeder's rights. CAN'T: reach beneficial owners offshore. FOR: one commission covers both company structure and trait ownership, which is unusually convenient.

trackers.name: PAIA request route — SAHRC
trackers.desc: The Human Rights Commission oversees the Promotion of Access to Information Act, including guidance and complaints. CAN: use a statutory route to request executive-council records and decision files. CAN'T: compel disclosure without escalation. FOR: PAIA reaches private bodies as well as public ones, which is rare and useful here.

trackers.name: Biowatch South Africa
trackers.desc: Organisation working on biosafety, seed sovereignty and smallholder farming, and party to a landmark costs judgment on public-interest litigation. CAN: reach both the seed-network practice and the litigation history. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: their costs ruling changed the risk calculus for public-interest environmental litigation across South Africa.

trackers.name: African Centre for Biodiversity — seed and farmer support
trackers.desc: The seed-systems arm of the continent's leading independent research organisation on this subject, working on farmer seed systems and against seed-law harmonisation. CAN: get country-level analysis of seed law across Africa, and the practical farmer-seed material. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: African seed-law harmonisation is being decided now and there is very little independent analysis of it; this is most of what exists.

trackers.name: Free State Department of Agriculture and Rural Development
trackers.desc: The provincial agriculture department for South Africa's main maize province. CAN: reach provincial agricultural administration and extension. CAN'T: decide GMO Act permits, which are national. FOR: South Africa grows GM white maize as a staple food crop rather than as feed — which is close to unique globally — and most of it is grown here.

trackers.name: National Biosafety Authority
trackers.desc: Kenya's competent authority: applications and approvals for contained use, confined field trials and environmental release, plus the public-participation notices that accompany them. CAN: find live applications and the consultation notices attached to them. CAN'T: settle the contested legal status of Kenya's import position, which has moved through the courts. FOR: Kenya is a bellwether for the region — what is approved here tends to shape neighbouring frameworks.

trackers.name: Kenya Law
trackers.desc: Official free case law and legislation. CAN: read the petitions over the GMO import ban and its lifting, which have run through the courts repeatedly. CAN'T: cover tribunal matters fully. FOR: Kenya's GMO position has been decided and re-decided in court as much as in cabinet.

trackers.name: Kenya Peasants League / Route to Food
trackers.desc: Food-systems initiative publishing research on Kenyan agricultural policy, pesticide and seed law. CAN: get independent Kenyan analysis of seed law and biosafety decisions. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: East African seed-law harmonisation is being decided now, and there is little independent analysis of it.

trackers.name: National Biosafety Management Agency (NBMA)
trackers.desc: Nigeria's competent authority for permits covering contained use, confined trials and commercial release, with public notices of applications received. CAN: see applications and permits, and the notice periods attached to them. CAN'T: be assumed complete — publication has been uneven. FOR: Nigeria has approved releases faster than most of the region, and the notice periods are short, so monitoring matters more than usual here.

trackers.name: Health of Mother Earth Foundation (HOMEF)
trackers.desc: Nigerian ecological think tank running sustained monitoring of NBMA permits and biosafety law. CAN: get the objection record and technical critique for Nigerian approvals, which are otherwise almost undocumented. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Nigeria approves quickly with short notice periods, and HOMEF is effectively the only continuous public watch on it.

trackers.name: Corporate Affairs Commission
trackers.desc: Nigeria's company registry. CAN: identify the corporate parties behind permit applications. CAN'T: reach beneficial ownership reliably. FOR: applications frequently name local subsidiaries whose parentage is not stated on the permit.

trackers.name: Federal Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: The ministry above Nigeria's biosafety agency. CAN: reach the environmental policy framework and the ministry that oversees the agency issuing permits. CAN'T: substitute for the agency on permits themselves. FOR: where an agency approves quickly, the supervising ministry is the next place a complaint goes.

trackers.name: Bureau of Plant Industry — biotech applications
trackers.desc: The Philippine biotechnology approval process for field trials, propagation and direct use, including the public-notice stage that Philippine rules require. CAN: find applications at notice stage, when objection is still possible. CAN'T: be treated as stable — the Philippine framework has been rewritten following litigation. FOR: the Philippines is where a national court has actually halted approvals on procedural grounds, which makes its record unusually instructive.

trackers.name: MASIPAG
trackers.desc: Farmer-led network of scientists and smallholders running farmer-managed seed banks and participatory breeding as a direct alternative to proprietary seed. CAN: reach a working, decades-old model of farmer seed sovereignty, and the people running it. CAN'T: act as a regulatory record. FOR: the defensive half of this map — keeping an unmodified line alive in farmers' hands — has few better working examples anywhere.

trackers.name: Supreme Court E-Library
trackers.desc: Official Philippine case law. CAN: read the decisions that halted GM field trials and then reshaped the national biosafety framework. CAN'T: cover lower-court matters. FOR: the Philippines is one of very few countries where a national court has actually stopped approvals on procedural and precautionary grounds.

trackers.name: SEC Philippines
trackers.desc: Company registration and filings. CAN: identify the corporate parties behind Philippine biotechnology applications. CAN'T: reach unregistered partnerships. FOR: several of the region's contested trials run through local joint ventures.

trackers.name: Japan Biosafety Clearing House (J-BCH)
trackers.desc: Japan's national biosafety clearing house: approvals under the Cartagena Act for Type 1 (environmental) and Type 2 (contained) use, in Japanese and English. CAN: find approved organisms and the ministry that approved them. CAN'T: cover food approvals, which run separately through the food-safety system. FOR: Japan approves a very large number of events for import while cultivating almost none — a useful demonstration that approval and cultivation are separable policy choices.

trackers.name: MAFF — biotechnology
trackers.desc: Japan's agriculture ministry, handling Type 1 use approvals for GM plants and publishing the approved list. CAN: see what is approved for import, cultivation and feed use in one of the world's largest importing countries. CAN'T: cover food-safety assessment, which sits elsewhere. FOR: Japan approves a very large number of events while cultivating almost none — useful proof that approval and cultivation are separable.

trackers.name: Consumers Union of Japan
trackers.desc: Long-standing consumer organisation central to Japan's GM labelling regime and to the No! GMO campaign. CAN: get the history of how consumer pressure produced one of the world's stricter labelling systems. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Japan is the clearest case of consumer organisation shaping labelling law.

trackers.name: JPlatPat
trackers.desc: Japan's patent information platform, free and full-text. CAN: search patents over traits and events relevant to Japanese import approvals. CAN'T: cover unpublished applications. FOR: Japanese corporate filings on agricultural biotechnology are under-examined in English-language work.

trackers.name: Courts in Japan — judgment database
trackers.desc: The Japanese judiciary's published judgments. CAN: find the litigation over GM crop cultivation and labelling. CAN'T: be searched easily without Japanese. FOR: Japanese consumer litigation shaped one of the world's stricter labelling regimes, and the reasoning is public.

trackers.name: Food Safety Commission of Japan
trackers.desc: The independent body assessing food safety, including foods derived from genetic modification, publishing its assessments. CAN: read the food-safety reasoning separately from the environmental decision — they are different bodies in Japan. CAN'T: cover cultivation approval. FOR: separating the two assessments makes it easier to see which questions each actually asked.

trackers.name: Bioteknologirådet — Norwegian Biotechnology Advisory Board
trackers.desc: Independent public advisory body on biotechnology, publishing in English, whose remit explicitly includes ethical and social consequences alongside safety. CAN: get reasoned public assessments that address sustainability, benefit to society and ethics — criteria Norway's Gene Technology Act uniquely requires and most regimes exclude. CAN'T: authorise anything. FOR: when you want to argue that a regulator should be weighing more than molecular risk, Norway is the precedent that it can be done in law.

trackers.name: Norwegian Environment Agency
trackers.desc: The authority handling deliberate release under Norway's Gene Technology Act. CAN: see decisions made under a statute that requires benefit to society, sustainability and ethical justification alongside safety. CAN'T: apply to EU member states. FOR: Norway is the standing proof that a regulator can lawfully be required to weigh more than molecular risk.

trackers.name: GenØk — Centre for Biosafety
trackers.desc: An independent biosafety research institute doing risk assessment research and capacity-building, particularly with countries in the global South. CAN: reach independent scientific work on biosafety methodology, and training material used by regulators elsewhere. CAN'T: be a regulator. FOR: much of the technical critique of risk-assessment practice used worldwide originates from a handful of institutes, and this is one of them.

trackers.name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica
trackers.desc: Spain's competent authority for deliberate release, holding the national register of GMO releases and authorisations. CAN: find notified releases in the only EU member state cultivating GM maize at scale. CAN'T: be relied on for a clean machine-readable feed. FOR: Spain is the EU's cultivation exception, which makes its register the most consequential in Europe.

trackers.name: Amigos de la Tierra España
trackers.desc: Friends of the Earth Spain, which has tracked Spanish GM maize cultivation and contamination for two decades. CAN: get the Spanish contamination and coexistence record, largely absent from official sources. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Spain publishes cultivation totals but almost nothing on coexistence failures; this is where those are documented.

trackers.name: Portal de Transparencia
trackers.desc: Spain's national transparency portal and request route. CAN: request release notifications, coexistence records and inspection data. CAN'T: reach autonomous-community bodies in every case. FOR: coexistence enforcement in Spain is regional, so expect to file more than once.

trackers.name: CENDOJ — Spanish judicial documentation centre
trackers.desc: Free search of Spanish court decisions at every level. CAN: find the litigation over GM maize cultivation, coexistence rules and regional GM-free declarations. CAN'T: cover administrative decisions that were never appealed. FOR: Spain cultivates GM maize commercially, so its coexistence case law is the most developed in the EU.

trackers.name: Sede Electrónica del Catastro
trackers.desc: Spain's cadastre, with free parcel search and mapping. CAN: identify parcels and their use around a cultivation site in the EU's main GM-growing member state. CAN'T: give ownership names without a justified request. FOR: Spanish coexistence disputes turn on distances between parcels, and this is where those distances are measured.

trackers.name: Gobierno de Aragón — agriculture
trackers.desc: The regional government of Aragón, which together with Catalonia accounts for most of the EU's commercial GM maize. CAN: reach regional agricultural administration and the coexistence rules applied on the ground. CAN'T: cover EU authorisation.
