FOR: almost all GM cultivation in the European Union happens in two Spanish regions, and this is one of them — which makes regional coexistence enforcement the whole of Europe's practical experience.

trackers.name: Generalitat de Catalunya — Acció Climàtica i Alimentació
trackers.desc: The Catalan agriculture and food department. CAN: reach regional coexistence rules, cultivation declarations and the organic certification system alongside them. CAN'T: cover EU authorisation. FOR: the other half of the EU's GM cultivation, and the region with the most developed public record of coexistence disputes between neighbouring growers.

trackers.name: Ministero dell'Ambiente
trackers.desc: Italy's competent authority for deliberate release. CAN: reach the national framework in a country that has consistently refused GM cultivation. CAN'T: be treated as an active release register — there is little to register. FOR: Italy's refusal is a worked example of a member state using the EU opt-out.

trackers.name: Normattiva
trackers.desc: Official consolidated Italian legislation. CAN: read the national instruments prohibiting or restricting GM cultivation. CAN'T: cover case law. FOR: the legal text of an opt-out is the model other regions copy.

trackers.name: ISPRA — Italian Institute for Environmental Protection and Research
trackers.desc: The national environmental research and protection institute, which contributes to GMO risk assessment and environmental monitoring. CAN: reach the technical side of the Italian position and its biodiversity monitoring data. CAN'T: issue permits. FOR: Italy refuses cultivation politically; ISPRA is where the ecological reasoning behind that sits.

trackers.name: RIVM — GMO Office (Bureau GGO)
trackers.desc: The Netherlands' technical body for genetically modified organisms, advising on contained use and deliberate release. CAN: get the technical assessment basis for Dutch permits, published in detail. CAN'T: issue permits itself. FOR: Dutch assessments are published more fully than most and are a useful comparator.

trackers.name: Woo-verzoek — Rijksoverheid
trackers.desc: Dutch government portal, including the route for open-government (Woo) requests. CAN: request permit files and advisory correspondence. CAN'T: overcome commercial-confidence refusals. FOR: the Netherlands hosts substantial contained-use activity that never appears in a release register.

trackers.name: Netherlands Chamber of Commerce (KVK)
trackers.desc: The Dutch business register. CAN: identify company structure and officers for the seed and breeding companies headquartered in the Netherlands, several of which are among the largest in the world. CAN'T: be fully free for detailed extracts. FOR: the Dutch seed sector is disproportionately large, and a great deal of European breeding ownership resolves here.

trackers.name: Rechtspraak.nl
trackers.desc: The Dutch judiciary's free case-law database. CAN: find decisions on permits, environmental objections and the administrative-law route for challenging a GMO consent. CAN'T: cover unpublished first-instance matters. FOR: Dutch administrative-law procedure on environmental permits is well documented and frequently borrowed elsewhere in Europe.

trackers.name: Kadaster
trackers.desc: The Dutch land registry and mapping agency. CAN: resolve a site to parcels and owners. CAN'T: be free for full title extracts. FOR: the Netherlands hosts a dense concentration of breeding and trial sites in a small area, which makes adjacency analysis unusually productive here.

trackers.name: COGEM — Netherlands Commission on Genetic Modification
trackers.desc: The independent statutory body advising the Dutch government on genetic modification, publishing its advice in full and in English. CAN: read detailed technical advice on specific applications, plus the horizon-scanning reports that flag techniques before they reach a register. CAN'T: decide anything — it advises. FOR: COGEM publishes signalling reports on where the field is going, which is rare: most regulators only speak about what has already been applied for.

trackers.name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)
trackers.desc: Switzerland's competent authority for releases into the environment. CAN: find the framework and the terms of Switzerland's extended moratorium on GM cultivation. CAN'T: cover contained use in detail. FOR: Switzerland has renewed a national cultivation moratorium repeatedly by parliamentary decision — a mechanism worth studying.

trackers.name: Schweizer Allianz Gentechfrei
trackers.desc: The Swiss GM-free alliance, coordinating the coalition behind the moratorium renewals. CAN: get the political history of how a cultivation moratorium has been extended again and again. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: the most successful sustained national moratorium in Europe, documented by the people who ran it.

trackers.name: Swiss Federal Institute of Intellectual Property
trackers.desc: Switzerland's patent office. CAN: search patents over plants, traits and processes held by the agrochemical and seed companies headquartered there. CAN'T: cover European Patent Office oppositions in detail. FOR: two of the four agricultural biotechnology majors have deep Swiss roots, so a surprising share of the ownership record resolves here.

trackers.name: Ministry of Climate and Environment
trackers.desc: Poland's competent authority for GMO matters, holding the national registers of contained use and release. CAN: reach the framework in a large agricultural member state that restricts cultivation. CAN'T: be relied on for machine-readable data. FOR: Poland's restrictions sit alongside a very large farming sector, which makes the coexistence question concrete.

trackers.name: Swedish Board of Agriculture (Jordbruksverket)
trackers.desc: The competent authority for GM plants in Sweden, publishing field-trial notifications. CAN: find Swedish field-trial notifications and the conditions attached. CAN'T: cover contained use. FOR: Sweden runs more plant field trials than most of northern Europe, including forestry species.

trackers.name: Gene Technology Advisory Board (Gentekniknamnden)
trackers.desc: Sweden's independent advisory board on gene technology, publishing analysis in Swedish and English. CAN: get plain assessments of new techniques and their regulatory status, from a body whose remit includes ethics as well as safety. CAN'T: decide applications. FOR: Sweden took an early public position on how gene editing should be classified, and the reasoning is here rather than in a ministry statement.

trackers.name: Korea Biosafety Clearing House
trackers.desc: Korea's national biosafety clearing house, holding LMO approvals, import records and risk-assessment material. CAN: find approvals and import data for a country that imports GM feed and grain in very large volumes. CAN'T: cover cultivation, which is minimal. FOR: Korea publishes LMO import statistics in unusual detail, including unintentional release monitoring along transport routes.

trackers.name: DART — corporate disclosure
trackers.desc: Korea's electronic corporate disclosure system, the equivalent of EDGAR. CAN: read filings for Korean firms in seed, feed and biotechnology, including subsidiary structures. CAN'T: reach unlisted companies. FOR: Korea imports GM feed and grain at very large volume, and the importing companies file here.

trackers.name: KIPRIS — Korea patent information
trackers.desc: Free full-text search of Korean patents and utility models, with English interface. CAN: search patents over traits, detection methods and processing techniques. CAN'T: cover unpublished applications. FOR: Korean patents on GM detection methods are unusually well developed, which matters for the testing lens.

trackers.name: Korea Rural Development Administration — LMO
trackers.desc: The agricultural research administration, which handles LMO risk assessment for agricultural use and runs the post-release monitoring programme. CAN: reach Korea's environmental monitoring for unintentional LMO release along transport and processing routes — a systematic programme few countries run. CAN'T: be read easily without Korean. FOR: Korea actively looks for escaped LMOs around ports and feed mills and publishes what it finds, which is close to unique.

trackers.name: Department of Environment
trackers.desc: Bangladesh's competent authority under the biosafety rules, handling approvals for release. CAN: reach the framework governing the country that commercialised Bt brinjal, the first GM food crop released in South Asia. CAN'T: be relied on for a searchable register. FOR: Bangladesh is the region's precedent case, cited constantly in Indian and Philippine argument.

trackers.name: UBINIG
trackers.desc: Policy research and farmer-network organisation running the Nayakrishi Andolon seed network. CAN: reach an operating farmer seed system and the documented critique of the Bt brinjal rollout. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: the counter-account of South Asia's flagship release, from the farmers involved.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs
trackers.desc: China's competent authority, publishing biosafety certificate approvals for GM crops. CAN: track the certificate lists, which signal cultivation policy shifts before they are announced. CAN'T: be read without Chinese, and offers no English feed. FOR: China's approvals move the global market; the certificate lists are the earliest public signal.

trackers.name: CNIPA
trackers.desc: China's patent office. CAN: search patents over traits and events, and identify the state and private institutes holding them. CAN'T: be searched easily in English. FOR: the ownership map of Chinese agricultural biotechnology is substantially different from the Western one and is rarely examined.

trackers.name: Supreme People's Court — judgments online
trackers.desc: China's public judgment database. CAN: find seed-law, variety-rights and unauthorised-planting cases, which exist in numbers few outside China examine. CAN'T: be assumed complete; publication practice has varied. FOR: unauthorised planting of unapproved GM crops has been prosecuted in China, and the judgments are the record of it.

trackers.name: Uganda National Council for Science and Technology
trackers.desc: The body approving confined field trials in Uganda. CAN: reach the framework governing a country running confined trials for years without a biosafety law in force. CAN'T: be relied on for published trial detail. FOR: Uganda is the clearest example of trials proceeding while the enabling statute remains unresolved.

trackers.name: ULII — Uganda Legal Information Institute
trackers.desc: Free Ugandan legislation and case law. CAN: follow the constitutional and procedural challenges around Uganda's long-unresolved biosafety bill. CAN'T: cover administrative decisions. FOR: Uganda ran confined trials for years while the enabling statute went unsigned; the legal record of that is here.

trackers.name: National Biosafety Authority Ghana
trackers.desc: Ghana's competent authority, publishing permit applications and public notices. CAN: see applications at notice stage, when objection is still possible. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Ghana's approval of Bt cowpea is a West African precedent now cited across the region.

trackers.name: SAG — Servicio Agrícola y Ganadero
trackers.desc: Chile's agricultural authority, which authorises GM seed multiplication for export. CAN: reach the framework for a country that grows large volumes of GM seed for northern-hemisphere companies while barring GM cultivation for domestic consumption. CAN'T: be relied on for a public site register — locations have been treated as commercially confidential and litigated over. FOR: Chile is the clearest case of a country hosting production it does not permit its own farmers to grow.

trackers.name: Portal de Transparencia
trackers.desc: Chile's transparency portal and request route to every public body. CAN: request SAG authorisation records and the seed-multiplication site data. CAN'T: overcome a commercial-confidence claim without appealing to the Council for Transparency. FOR: the Chilean site-location question was won on transparency grounds, not biosafety grounds.

trackers.name: Poder Judicial de Chile
trackers.desc: Chile's judiciary, with case search. CAN: follow the litigation over disclosure of GM seed-multiplication site locations. CAN'T: cover administrative decisions unappealed. FOR: the Chilean site-location question was decided in litigation, and the reasoning is the transferable part.

trackers.name: ICA — Instituto Colombiano Agropecuario
trackers.desc: Colombia's agricultural authority, handling GM crop authorisations and seed registration. CAN: find authorisations and the seed rules that go with them. CAN'T: be treated as a searchable register. FOR: Colombian seed-certification rules have themselves been a major flashpoint for farmer organisations.

trackers.name: Grupo Semillas
trackers.desc: Colombian organisation on seed, biodiversity and farmers' rights, documenting GM authorisations and seed-law conflicts. CAN: get the Colombian record of contamination in native maize and the campesino legal position. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: Colombia sits at the southern edge of maize diversity, and this is who tracks it.

trackers.name: Corte Constitucional de Colombia
trackers.desc: Colombia's constitutional court. CAN: read the rulings on seed law, prior consultation with Indigenous and Afro-descendant communities, and the environmental precautionary principle. CAN'T: cover ordinary civil matters. FOR: Colombia's prior-consultation jurisprudence is among the strongest anywhere and applies directly to releases on or near collective territories.

trackers.name: SENASA Perú
trackers.desc: Peru's agricultural health service, which administers the moratorium on the entry and release of living modified organisms. CAN: reach the terms and administration of one of the longest national moratoria in the world. CAN'T: cover research under contained conditions, which continues. FOR: Peru extended its moratorium rather than letting it lapse — the mechanism and the politics are both worth studying.

trackers.name: Gabinete Nacional de Bioseguridad
trackers.desc: Uruguay's inter-ministerial biosafety body, handling authorisation of GM events for cultivation. CAN: reach the framework in a small country that grows GM soy and maize at scale relative to its size. CAN'T: be relied on for a structured register. FOR: Uruguay's coexistence rules for maize are among the more detailed in the region.

trackers.name: SENAVE
trackers.desc: Paraguay's plant health and seed quality service, which registers seed and controls its movement. CAN: reach seed registration and movement control in a major GM soy producer. CAN'T: substitute for the biosafety commission on approvals. FOR: Paraguay's GM soy expansion and its land-conflict record are closely linked, and seed registration is where the paper trail starts.

trackers.name: Servicio Fitosanitario del Estado
trackers.desc: Costa Rica's phytosanitary service, which handles GM crop permits, largely for seed multiplication for export. CAN: find the permit framework and the categories of authorised activity. CAN'T: be treated as a live register. FOR: several Costa Rican cantons have declared themselves GM-free, which makes the municipal layer unusually active here.

trackers.name: EPA Ireland — GMO regulation
trackers.desc: Ireland's competent authority for contained use and deliberate release. CAN: find notifications, consents and the public consultation notices attached to them. CAN'T: cover food and feed authorisation, which is EU-level. FOR: Ireland has hosted contested field trials while positioning itself as GM-free in policy — both threads run through this authority.

trackers.name: Companies Registration Office
trackers.desc: Ireland's company register with free company search and filed accounts. CAN: identify directors and group structure, including the Irish holding entities used by multinational agribusiness. CAN'T: reveal beneficial owners beyond the separate RBO. FOR: Irish holding structures appear in a surprising number of agricultural-biotechnology corporate trees.

trackers.name: Standards in Public Office Commission
trackers.desc: Ireland's ethics and lobbying regulator, running the lobbying register and publishing interest statements. CAN: see lobbying returns naming the official and the subject. CAN'T: cover unregistered contact. FOR: Ireland's register is comparatively strict and returns are filed three times a year.

trackers.name: Belgian Biosafety Server
trackers.desc: Belgium's biosafety information service, publishing contained-use and deliberate-release notifications with technical summaries in English. CAN: read notification summaries for a country hosting substantial plant biotechnology research. CAN'T: cover EU-level authorisation. FOR: Belgium publishes contained-use information more openly than most, which partly fills the largest recording gap on this map.

trackers.name: Belgian Biosafety Advisory Council
trackers.desc: The advisory council that issues opinions on Belgian and EU notifications, published with the reasoning. CAN: read opinions on contained use and deliberate release from a country hosting substantial plant biotechnology research. CAN'T: cover EU-level authorisation. FOR: Belgium publishes contained-use information more openly than most, which partly fills the largest recording gap on this map.

trackers.name: Miljøstyrelsen — Danish EPA
trackers.desc: Denmark's environmental protection agency, competent for deliberate release. CAN: reach notifications and the Danish coexistence rules, which include a compensation scheme for contamination losses. CAN'T: cover food approvals. FOR: Denmark operates one of the few statutory compensation funds for GM contamination of a neighbouring crop — a model worth citing elsewhere.

trackers.name: Retsinformation — Danish legislation
trackers.desc: The official database of Danish law. CAN: read the statutory compensation scheme for GM contamination of a neighbouring crop — one of very few in the world where the remedy is written into law rather than left to litigation. CAN'T: be searched without Danish. FOR: when the question is ‘what would compensation even look like’, this is the working answer to point at.

trackers.name: Ministry of the Environment
trackers.desc: The Czech competent authority, maintaining the registers of contained use and deliberate release. CAN: find the national registers and the notification framework. CAN'T: be relied on for English coverage. FOR: Czechia cultivated GM maize commercially and then stopped — the record of why is here.

trackers.name: Hungarian Government — agriculture
trackers.desc: Government portal covering the agriculture ministry, which administers Hungary's GMO-free policy. CAN: reach the framework of a country whose constitution commits it to GMO-free agriculture. CAN'T: be searched easily without Hungarian. FOR: Hungary is the only country to write a GMO-free commitment into its constitution; the implementing rules are the interesting part.

trackers.name: GMO portal (gmo.kormany.hu)
trackers.desc: Hungary's dedicated government GMO site, listed by the CBD as the national biosafety web address. CAN: reach the national rules implementing a constitutional commitment to GMO-free agriculture, in one place rather than across ministry pages. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: a country that put the commitment in its constitution had to write implementing rules to match, and this is where they sit.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Romania's competent authority for GMO matters, holding the national release registers. CAN: reach the framework in a country that cultivated GM soy before EU accession and stopped on joining. CAN'T: be relied on for structured data. FOR: Romania is the clearest case of accession law removing a cultivation practice, and of the pressure since to restore it.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry
trackers.desc: Turkey's competent authority under its biosafety law, which permits GM feed imports but bars GM cultivation. CAN: reach the approved-event list for feed and the cultivation prohibition. CAN'T: be searched easily without Turkish. FOR: Turkey is a large importer with a cultivation ban and criminal penalties attached — an unusual combination worth understanding.

trackers.name: BIOTEC — National Center for Genetic Engineering and Biotechnology
trackers.desc: Thailand's national biotechnology centre, which runs research and sits inside the biosafety framework. CAN: see the public research programme and its institutional links. CAN'T: act as the regulator — approvals run through the agriculture department. FOR: Thailand has maintained a field-trial restriction for years while research continues; both facts live here.

trackers.name: Department of Agriculture Thailand
trackers.desc: Thailand's agriculture department, which administers the plant quarantine controls under which GM field trials have been restricted for years. CAN: reach the quarantine framework, which is the actual legal mechanism behind Thailand's restriction. CAN'T: be searched easily without Thai. FOR: Thailand restricts trials through plant quarantine law rather than biosafety law — a mechanism worth understanding because it is available in many countries that lack a biosafety act.

trackers.name: Taiwan FDA — genetically modified food
trackers.desc: Taiwan's food regulator, holding the approved GM food ingredient list and the labelling rules. CAN: find approved events for food use and the labelling thresholds. CAN'T: cover cultivation, which is prohibited. FOR: Taiwan bans GM crops in school meals, which is a concrete municipal-scale policy lever used elsewhere.

trackers.name: National Biosafety Authority Zambia
trackers.desc: Zambia's competent authority for permits covering contained use, trials and release. CAN: reach the framework of a country that refused GM food aid in 2002 and built a biosafety regime afterwards. CAN'T: be assumed to publish completely. FOR: Zambia's refusal is the founding case in African biosafety politics and is still argued over.

trackers.name: ZambiaLII
trackers.desc: Free Zambian legislation and case law. CAN: read the biosafety act as enacted and any litigation under it. CAN'T: cover every tribunal. FOR: Zambia built its regime after refusing GM food aid, so the statute itself is the argument.

trackers.name: National Biosafety Authority (nbazambia.org.zm)
trackers.desc: Zambia's biosafety authority, at the address the CBD focal point list gives. CAN: reach permits, guidance and the regulatory framework built after Zambia refused GM food aid. CAN'T: be assumed to publish every decision. FOR: this is the current address; older references to a different domain should be treated as stale.

trackers.name: Ethiopian Environment Protection Authority
trackers.desc: Ethiopia's environmental authority, historically central to African negotiating positions on the Cartagena Protocol. CAN: reach the national framework of a country that led the African group in the biosafety negotiations. CAN'T: be relied on for permit-level detail. FOR: the African common position on biosafety was largely drafted out of Addis Ababa, and that history shapes the whole continent's law.

trackers.name: DGAV — Direcção-Geral de Alimentação e Veterinária
trackers.desc: Portugal's authority for GM crop cultivation, which maintains the register of parcels sown with GM maize. CAN: find the declared cultivation areas — Portugal is one of only two EU states cultivating GM maize commercially, and it publishes parcel-level declarations. CAN'T: cover EU-level authorisation. FOR: parcel declarations are the closest thing in Europe to a public map of where GM crops are actually growing.

trackers.name: Ministerio del Ambiente, Agua y Transición Ecológica
trackers.desc: Ecuador's environmental authority. CAN: reach the framework of a country whose constitution declares it free of transgenic seeds and crops, subject to narrow exceptions. CAN'T: be relied on for a permit register — there is little to register. FOR: Ecuador wrote the prohibition into its constitution, which makes it the strongest national text of its kind and a model other movements cite.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Environment
trackers.desc: Vietnam's competent authority for biosafety, handling biodiversity-safety certificates for GM crops. CAN: reach the national framework in a country that approved GM maize for cultivation and imports feed at scale. CAN'T: be searched easily without Vietnamese. FOR: Vietnam is one of the few Southeast Asian countries to have approved cultivation rather than import only.

trackers.name: Ministry of Climate Change & Environmental Coordination
trackers.desc: Pakistan's federal environment ministry, which houses the National Biosafety Centre. CAN: reach the federal framework, and the question of whether biosafety authority sits federally or provincially — unresolved since devolution. CAN'T: be relied on for permit-level publication. FOR: Pakistan grows Bt cotton on a very large area with a contested approval history and almost no public record of it.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture — Plant Protection and Inspection Services
trackers.desc: Israel's plant health authority, which oversees GM field trials. CAN: reach the framework of a country with substantial agricultural biotechnology research and effectively no commercial GM cultivation. CAN'T: be searched easily without Hebrew. FOR: a large research base with no commercial release is an unusual combination and a useful comparator.

trackers.name: Board for Gene Technology
trackers.desc: Finland's gene technology board sits under the social affairs and health ministry and handles contained use and deliberate release. CAN: reach the national framework and notification route. CAN'T: cover EU-level authorisation. FOR: Finland runs forestry-species research, which is where the perennial, wind-pollinated, long-lived risk profile bites hardest.

trackers.name: Finnish Food Authority (Ruokavirasto)
trackers.desc: The national food authority, which runs seed certification and GM testing of food and feed. CAN: reach official testing and the seed certification system. CAN'T: authorise releases, which sit with the gene technology board. FOR: Finland's forestry research makes it one of the places engineered trees are actually studied, and seed certification is where that meets the market.

trackers.name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Spatial Planning
trackers.desc: Slovenia's government portal, covering the ministry competent for GMO matters and the national registers. CAN: reach the framework of a member state that has declared much of its territory GM-free at regional level. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Slovenia's regional GM-free declarations are among the densest in Europe relative to national area.

trackers.name: Department of Biosafety Malaysia
trackers.desc: Malaysia's competent authority under its biosafety act, publishing approvals and public-consultation notices. CAN: find applications at notice stage. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Malaysia ran one of the region's early engineered-mosquito trials, and its consultation notices are the record of how that was handled.

trackers.name: Indonesian Biosafety Clearing House
trackers.desc: Indonesia's national biosafety clearing house, holding release approvals and risk assessments. CAN: reach approvals in the largest country in Southeast Asia, including for engineered sugarcane. CAN'T: be assumed complete or current. FOR: Indonesia approved domestically developed engineered crops rather than imported events, which is an unusual and under-examined route.

trackers.name: Indonesian Biotechnology Information Centre
trackers.desc: The national biotechnology information node. CAN: reach the Indonesian research and approval picture. CAN'T: be treated as independent — information centres of this kind are generally industry-aligned, and the trust filters here mark it accordingly. FOR: included as a record rather than a voice, because for several Southeast Asian countries it is the only consolidated public account that exists.

trackers.name: Ministry of Rural Development and Food
trackers.desc: Greece's competent authority for GMO matters in agriculture. CAN: reach the framework of a member state that has consistently used the EU opt-out to bar GM cultivation. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Greece is one of the member states that opted out of cultivation across its whole territory.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Water Management
trackers.desc: Serbia's agriculture ministry. CAN: reach the framework of a country whose law prohibits the commercial cultivation and trade of GMOs outright — a position under continuous pressure from accession negotiations. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Serbia is the clearest live case of a national prohibition being weighed against trade-liberalisation pressure.

trackers.name: Plant Protection Directorate — biosafety group
trackers.desc: The directorate inside Serbia's agriculture ministry that holds plant variety protection and biosafety, named by the CBD as the national focal point. CAN: reach the office that actually administers the prohibition, rather than the ministry above it. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: when a country prohibits outright, the interesting documents are about enforcement and about the pressure to change it — both sit at directorate level.

trackers.name: National Environment Management Council
trackers.desc: Tanzania's environmental authority, competent under its biosafety regulations. CAN: reach the framework of a country whose regulations imposed strict liability on researchers and developers for any damage from a release. CAN'T: be relied on for published permit detail. FOR: Tanzania's strict-liability clause was the most demanding in Africa and its subsequent relaxation is a documented case of regulatory pressure working.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment and Water
trackers.desc: Bulgaria's competent authority for GMO matters. CAN: reach the framework of a member state with one of the strictest national GMO laws in the EU, including buffer zones around protected areas. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Bulgaria's law bans cultivation near protected areas and organic farms by distance — a mechanism worth copying.

trackers.name: Department of Environment
trackers.desc: Cyprus's environment department inside the agriculture ministry, the national focal point for biosafety. CAN: reach the framework in a small member state with a substantial seed and plant trade. CAN'T: cover EU-level authorisation. FOR: island states have coexistence problems that continental rules were not written for, and the departmental level is where that shows.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Lithuania's competent ministry for GMO matters. CAN: reach national notification and register rules. CAN'T: be relied on for English throughout. FOR: the Baltic states have very little independent civil-society capacity on this subject, which makes the official framework the whole of the public record.

trackers.name: Ministry of Agriculture
trackers.desc: Latvia's agriculture ministry, whose food safety and genetic engineering division is the national focal point. CAN: reach the national framework and the coexistence rules. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Latvia allows municipalities to declare themselves GM-free, and a large share have — the mechanism is in the national rules.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment — environmental risk & biosafety
trackers.desc: Slovakia's competent ministry, whose department of environmental risk and biosafety is the focal point. CAN: reach the notification framework and national registers. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: Slovakia cultivated GM maize commercially and then stopped; the record of the wind-down sits here.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment and Physical Planning
trackers.desc: North Macedonia's competent ministry, with a division specifically on biodiversity and genetically modified organisms. CAN: reach the framework of a candidate country aligning its law with the EU. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: accession alignment is where national prohibitions get renegotiated, and the process is public.

trackers.name: Ministry of Economy, Environment and Agriculture
trackers.desc: Ukraine's combined economy, environment and agriculture ministry, whose biosafety division is the national focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a major grain exporter. CAN'T: be assumed current given the circumstances. FOR: Ukraine's grain exports move through markets with very different GM rules, which makes its own position consequential well beyond its borders.

trackers.name: National Parks Board
trackers.desc: Singapore's National Parks Board, the biosafety focal point, which also runs the genetic modification advisory framework. CAN: reach the framework of a major transhipment hub with a large biotechnology research base and almost no agriculture. CAN'T: offer a cultivation register — there is nothing to cultivate. FOR: transhipment states shape what moves through the region, and their rules are rarely examined.

trackers.name: CONAP — Consejo Nacional de Áreas Protegidas
trackers.desc: Guatemala's protected areas council, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country inside the Mesoamerican centre of maize diversity. CAN'T: be relied on for permit-level publication. FOR: Guatemala repealed a seed law after mass protest, which makes it one of the clearest cases of a seed statute being defeated outright.

trackers.name: Ministerio de Ambiente
trackers.desc: Panama's environment ministry, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country whose canal makes it a chokepoint for grain movement between the Americas and Asia. CAN'T: be relied on for a release register. FOR: what transits matters as much as what is grown, and Panama sees a large share of it.

trackers.name: Environment Public Authority
trackers.desc: Kuwait's environment authority, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a Gulf state importing essentially all of its food. CAN'T: offer a cultivation register. FOR: import-dependent states set the labelling and approval rules that exporters have to satisfy, which gives them leverage they rarely use.

trackers.name: Environment Protection Agency (EPA-SL)
trackers.desc: Sierra Leone's environment agency, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a country with very little published biosafety material otherwise. CAN'T: be assumed to hold a permit register. FOR: for much of West Africa the agency page is the entire public record, and knowing that is better than assuming more exists.

trackers.name: Bhutan Food and Drug Authority
trackers.desc: Bhutan's food and drug authority, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country that has built agricultural policy around organic production. CAN'T: be assumed comprehensive. FOR: Bhutan is the clearest national case of an agricultural policy that makes GM cultivation moot rather than prohibited.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Lebanon's environment ministry, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a country sitting inside the Fertile Crescent, a centre of origin for wheat and barley. CAN'T: be assumed current. FOR: centre-of-origin status is the argument, and the wheat and barley centre is less discussed than the maize one.

trackers.name: Agence Nationale de Biosécurité
trackers.desc: Burkina Faso's national biosafety agency. CAN: reach the framework of the country that hosted the world's most advanced engineered-mosquito programme, and then stopped it. CAN'T: be assumed to publish every decision. FOR: after a trial release at Souroukoudingan on 11 August 2025, the government sealed Target Malaria's facilities on 18 August and suspended all of its activities on 22 August. Burkina Faso had already withdrawn from Bt cotton after the fibre-quality losses. Twice now a host government has ended a flagship programme on its own terms, which is not the usual direction of travel.

trackers.name: Terre à Vie / COPAGEN Burkina
trackers.desc: Farmer and civil-society organisation active in the opposition to Bt cotton and to the engineered-mosquito releases. CAN: reach the organising and the documentation behind two of the most significant reversals in African biotechnology. CAN'T: act as an official record. FOR: the Bt cotton withdrawal is usually told as a technical failure over fibre length; the account from the farmer organisations is different and worth reading alongside it.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment — Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency
trackers.desc: Egypt's environmental affairs agency, the national biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework in the largest wheat importer in the world. CAN'T: be relied on for a permit register. FOR: what a country of that import volume accepts sets the standard exporters have to meet, which gives importing states leverage they rarely use.

trackers.name: Ministère de la Transition Énergétique et du Développement Durable
trackers.desc: Morocco's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework. CAN'T: be assumed to publish decisions. FOR: Morocco is a significant seed-multiplication location for European companies, which is a quieter form of the same industry.

trackers.name: Ministère de l'Environnement
trackers.desc: Tunisia's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country with a legal prohibition on GMO cultivation. CAN'T: be relied on for English. FOR: North African prohibitions are less discussed than European ones and rest on different legal grounds.

trackers.name: Direction de l'Environnement et des Établissements Classés
trackers.desc: Senegal's environment directorate, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a West African country that has held back from commercial GM release while neighbours moved. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Senegal's farmer organisations are among the strongest in the region, and the contrast with Burkina Faso and Ghana is instructive.

trackers.name: Agence Nationale de la Gestion des Stations d'Épuration
trackers.desc: Mali's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework. CAN'T: be assumed current. FOR: Mali sits in the Sahelian cotton belt beside Burkina Faso, whose Bt cotton withdrawal reshaped the regional argument.

trackers.name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Protection de la Nature
trackers.desc: Cameroon's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a country with substantial cotton and cocoa sectors. CAN'T: be assumed to publish permits. FOR: Central African biosafety frameworks are the least documented anywhere and this is the entry point.

trackers.name: Ministério da Terra e Ambiente
trackers.desc: Mozambique's land and environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country that ran confined trials of drought-tolerant maize. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Mozambique changed its biosafety regulations to permit confined trials after previously prohibiting them, which is the pattern the region is following.

trackers.name: Environmental Affairs Department
trackers.desc: Malawi's environmental affairs department, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of one of the first southern African countries after South Africa to approve Bt cotton commercially. CAN'T: be assumed to publish decisions. FOR: Malawi's approval is cited across the region as precedent.

trackers.name: National Biotechnology Authority of Zimbabwe
trackers.desc: Zimbabwe's biotechnology authority, which regulates both research and imports. CAN: reach the framework of a country that has maintained a prohibition on GM cultivation while permitting some processed imports. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Zimbabwe refused GM food aid alongside Zambia and has kept the position far longer than most.

trackers.name: Department of Environmental Affairs
trackers.desc: Botswana's environmental affairs department, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework. CAN'T: be assumed to hold a register. FOR: Botswana's beef export trade to the EU makes its position on GM feed commercially consequential in a way most of its neighbours' is not.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment, Forestry and Tourism
trackers.desc: Namibia's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country with a biosafety act and a labelling requirement. CAN'T: be assumed to publish permits. FOR: Namibia legislated labelling early, which is unusual in the region.

trackers.name: Central Environmental Authority
trackers.desc: Sri Lanka's environmental authority, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country that attempted a nationwide agrochemical prohibition and reversed it. CAN'T: be assumed to hold a GM register. FOR: Sri Lanka is the clearest recent case of an abrupt agricultural policy shift and its consequences, which is argued about in every direction.

trackers.name: Ministry of Forests and Environment
trackers.desc: Nepal's forests and environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a country whose seed supply depends heavily on Indian imports. CAN'T: be assumed to publish decisions. FOR: import dependence means Nepal inherits decisions made in Delhi, which is a common and under-examined situation.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Cambodia's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework. CAN'T: be assumed complete. FOR: Mekong-region seed movement crosses borders informally at scale, which makes national frameworks partly notional and worth understanding as such.

trackers.name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environmental Conservation
trackers.desc: Myanmar's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the stated national framework. CAN'T: be assumed functional given the circumstances. FOR: recorded so the gap is visible rather than absent — a country with no working register is a different thing from a country not yet added.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Jordan's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the framework of a country inside the Fertile Crescent, a centre of origin for wheat and barley. CAN'T: be assumed to publish permits. FOR: the wheat and barley centre of origin spans several countries that are rarely discussed together; this is one.

trackers.name: Ministry of Local Administration and Environment
trackers.desc: Syria's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the stated framework. CAN'T: be assumed current. FOR: ICARDA's genebank was evacuated from Aleppo and became the first withdrawal from the Svalbard vault — the clearest demonstration anywhere of why duplicated seed storage exists.

trackers.name: Ministry of Environment
trackers.desc: Iraq's environment ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the stated framework. CAN'T: be assumed functional. FOR: Iraq sits at the heart of the wheat and barley centre of origin, and its seed system was substantially reorganised under occupation — a documented case of seed law being rewritten from outside.

trackers.name: Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources
trackers.desc: Azerbaijan's ecology ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework, in English. CAN'T: be assumed to publish permits. FOR: the Caucasus holds substantial crop diversity and almost no independent monitoring of it.

trackers.name: Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources
trackers.desc: Kazakhstan's ecology ministry, the biosafety focal point. CAN: reach the national framework in a major grain exporter. CAN'T: be assumed to hold a register. FOR: Kazakh wheat moves into markets with very different GM rules, which makes its own position consequential beyond its borders.
